observations: Two black power banks lying on a concrete floor.
The top power bank has a protective layer of yellowish tape on its front face.
Both units have charging cables attached: one green braided, one blue braided.
The top unit appears to have a small hole or cutout on the top edge.
The bottom unit shows some surface scratches and scuffs.
No brand names, logos, or model numbers are visible on the devices.

claims.evidence: The items appear used and may be non-functional.
The seller's location is not confirmed by the photos.

claims.claim: Battery is new, holds charge for 8 hours. Never repaired.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The batteries may be dead or unable to hold a charge.
risks.proof: A video showing a phone successfully charging from the power bank.

risks.risk: The internal capacity (mAh) is unknown, affecting resale value.
risks.proof: A photo of the manufacturer's label on the back of the device.
risks.if_unproven: as the lowest capacity common for this form factor

risks.risk: The cables may be damaged or have poor connectors.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the cable connectors and a video of the cables being tested.

proof_requests: Photo of the label on the back of the power banks showing the brand and capacity.
Video of a phone charging from the power bank.
Close-up photo of the cable connectors.
response.reason: The items are clearly identifiable as power banks. While their functional state is unverified, they can be priced at their worst-case value as non-functional scrap units.
